hints.title: Strict ID Ordering to Avoid Duplicates
hints.text: Join Points p1 with Points p2 on p1.id < p2.id to ensure each unordered point pair is examined exactly once.

hints.title: Non-Degenerate Rectangle Filter
hints.text: A valid rectangle requires p1.x_value <> p2.x_value and p1.y_value <> p2.y_value.

hints.title: Area Computation and Ordering
hints.text: Compute abs(p1.x_value - p2.x_value) * abs(p1.y_value - p2.y_value) as area, ordered by area desc, p1 asc, p2 asc.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT p1.id AS p1, p2.id AS p2,
       ABS(p1.x_value - p2.x_value) * ABS(p1.y_value - p2.y_value) AS area
FROM Points p1
JOIN Points p2 ON p1.id < p2.id
              AND p1.x_value != p2.x_value
              AND p1.y_value != p2.y_value
ORDER BY area DESC, p1 ASC, p2 ASC;
```

variables: N: number of points in Points table
complexity.notes: Testing all unordered pairs of points executes in quadratic time with secondary sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full Cartesian product without id ordering creates symmetric duplicates and zero-area pairs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Condition p1.id < p2.id halves pair comparisons and guarantees unique representation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Self-join with triangle condition p1.id < p2.id and non-zero dimension predicates.

SELECT p1.id AS p1, p2.id AS p2,
       ABS(p1.x_value - p2.x_value) * ABS(p1.y_value - p2.y_value) AS area
FROM Points p1
JOIN Points p2 ON p1.id < p2.id
              AND p1.x_value != p2.x_value
              AND p1.y_value != p2.y_value
ORDER BY area DESC, p1 ASC, p2 ASC;

import pandas as pd

def rectangles_area(points: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    merged = pd.merge(points, points, how='cross', suffixes=('_1', '_2'))
    filtered = merged[(merged['id_1'] < merged['id_2']) &
                      (merged['x_value_1'] != merged['x_value_2']) &
                      (merged['y_value_1'] != merged['y_value_2'])].copy()
    filtered['area'] = (filtered['x_value_1'] - filtered['x_value_2']).abs() * (filtered['y_value_1'] - filtered['y_value_2']).abs()
    filtered.rename(columns={'id_1': 'p1', 'id_2': 'p2'}, inplace=True)
    return filtered[['p1', 'p2', 'area']].sort_values(by=['area', 'p1', 'p2'], ascending=[False, True, True])
